readout_other: TMS MEP amplitude, brainstem MEP, RMT, SICI, ICF, SICF, I-O curve
direction_notes: DPS5 (200 Hz PRF) increased M1 MEP amplitude and DPS100 (10 Hz PRF) decreased it, both lasting 60-90 min; no change in brainstem MEP, RMT, SICI, ICF or SICF.
safety_notes: No adverse effects reported; estimated brain temperature rise 0.002-0.013 C.

exposures.label: DPS5 and DPS100 over M1 hotspot

target.label: motor cortex hotspot (right FDI representation, left M1)

timing.protocol_description: DPS5: 400-s train of ten 2-ms pulses repeated every 5 ms (PRF 200 Hz) as a decapulse, repeated at 1 Hz; DPS100: 2-ms pulses every 100 ms (PRF 10 Hz) for 4000 pulses. Net sonication 8 s in both; total time 400 s.

source_quotes.n_subjects: Thirteen right-handed healthy subjects (10 male, 3 female; age range 28–70 years; 51.3 ± 15.4 years (mean age ± standard deviation [SD])) participated after giving informed consent. None had neurological or psychiatric disorders or were on medications affecting brain excitability nor was there any risk of epileptic seizure or contraindications for TMS or TUS. The study followed the Declaration of Helsinki and was approved by Kyorin University’s Ethics Committee (approval number: R03–015–01).
